doc.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: The decline of permanent working groups
summary: They discuss how rising travel costs mean leaders hire local players instead of touring with a whole group.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: You know you mentioned something that I’ve been hearing lately and that is that it’s hard to have a cohesive group of musicians that you can get an ensemble sound and some rehearsed stuff. That’s a real shame.

It is. And it’s happened more in the last ten, fifteen years, that I guess the cost of flying has gotten more and more expensive. Because there are several people that I work with that say well we’d love to take the group, but then end up having to go themselves and then pick up musicians. They get very fine musicians generally, but there is still something different when you’re just thrust together with somebody, as to when you get to work and play together some and get a real group ensemble sound happening. But it just seems to be kind of a problem nowadays. It’s rare to see somebody take a whole quartet or quintet and travel with them.
